strengths: Clean five-habit structure delivered through one character, with a stat per habit.
Most figures match primary-style sources (AAA, Vanguard, BLS, Fed).
Strong contrarian opening (behaviour test, not an investment test).
weaknesses: The hook promise of "hundreds of thousands in ten years" is not delivered.
Thumbnail icons do not map to the habits and omit the $8,000.
The second half repeats the five habits twice.
contradictions: Title's "rule" is the stress-test habit, but the closing presents five questions as the rule.
Hook horizon (10 years) versus the later 30-year computation.
"MAKE THESE HABITS!" with exercise and reading icons versus five financial habits.
After the $2,400 repair paid from $8,312, Rain "keeps the $8,000" at the dealership and later stress-tests $8,000 as intact.
improvement_opportunities: Reword the hook to "$8,000 in the right order can become $610,000" and show the $500 a month, 30-year line on screen at ~1,000 characters.
Match the thumbnail icons to the five habits (emergency shield, car key, auto-transfer arrow, raise arrow, stress gauge) and add "$8,000".
Define the $8,000 rule once at the start in one sentence and use only that definition later.
Cut the second and third recaps (about 4,000 characters).
End with one ask tied to the content (set up the automatic transfer after your next payday) and a subscribe line.
